name: Rangreth

queries.query: Rangreth Srinagar official cadastral map land records parcel map Jammu Kashmir
queries.result: First-party discovery identified the Government of Jammu and Kashmir Revenue Department JKLR viewer, the National Government Services Portal description of the J&K LRIS GIS land-records system, and District Srinagar government land-records/map pages. The JKLR viewer's current JavaScript revealed authenticated API routes, but no anonymous parcel response was available.

queries.query: رنگریٹھ سرینگر سرکاری اراضی ریکارڈ نقشہ
queries.result: The native-language discovery query did not identify a Rangreth-specific first-party parcel endpoint. It reinforced the J&K land-records/cadastral-map route but returned unrelated or general land-records pages; no safe parcel ID-plus-geometry response was found.

registryEvidence.custodian: The J&K Revenue Department / JaKLaRMA is evidenced as the UT land-records custodian by the official JKLR viewer and National Government Services Portal description. District Srinagar government pages provide local administrative context, but not a city-local anonymous parcel API.
registryEvidence.scope: The official JKLR application is a current public-facing viewer shell, while its data API requires authentication. DoLR status pages show Srinagar cadastral maps and land parcels are digitized/georeferenced, but those progress reports do not provide parcel geometry or a public Rangreth endpoint.
registryEvidence.scopeNote: registryFound remains null because no local public registry/cadastre/map endpoint with inspectable safe parcel data was reached in this attempt. This is not evidence of citywide absence.

parcelDiscovery.source: Official J&K Revenue JKLR viewer and related government land-records references; a separate public ArcGIS planning service was inspected only for bounded schema/extent evidence and was not admitted as the registry source.

attemptedRoutes.outcome: HTTP 200 HTML received. Current JavaScript/configuration was fetched; API base was identified as https://d14fnjoywemmi.cloudfront.net/jklr-api and the app exposed routes such as get-districts, get-tehsil-by-district, get-village-by-tehsil, and get-khasra-by-khasra-id. No parcel geometry was present in the shell.
Anonymous bounded POST with an empty JSON body returned HTTP 401 Unauthorized. No credentials, token, login, CAPTCHA/Cloudflare bypass, or private access was attempted.
Anonymous bounded TLS GET timed out without an HTTP response. No login wall was bypassed and no TLS verification exception was used.

A public ArcGIS planning-service layer named Parcel returned HTTP 200 metadata with polygon geometry, CRS EPSG:32643, and extent [476033.0248,3612171.6129] to [493516.3586,3629749.0651]. Its schema includes unsafe ownership, address, telephone, Aadhaar, email, tax and other personal/property fields; no feature query was issued or retained. The extent does not cover the WUP point, and this was not treated as an absence finding or registry admission.
Government of India DoLR progress page returned Srinagar totals showing digitized/georeferenced cadastral maps and parcel counts, but no parcel IDs or geometry.

parcelDiscovery.note: The exact WUP point [34.0207106014512, 74.8014402245299] was preserved and not shifted to force a hit. No exact-point query or citywide absence inference was made. No unsafe source attributes or geometry were retained.

uncertainty: The official JKLR viewer's data APIs are authenticated and the alternate landrecords.jk.gov.in host timed out during this attempt; additional public routes may exist outside the observed shell.
The public ArcGIS layer is planning/property data rather than proven J&K Revenue cadastral custody and exposed unsafe fields, so it was not used for parcel retention.
A timeout, HTTP 401, extent miss, or zero exact-point hit is transport/access evidence only and is not evidence that Rangreth lacks cadastral coverage.
Packet completion is not source integration or runtime adapter admission.
